thread:
sara-support: Customer (Acme Mobile) reporting repeated mid-stream disconnects for streaming SSE. They get partial output then connection drops, sometimes billing for partial tokens. Request ID: req_0a1b2c. SDK: js-client v1.4.2. App: Android 12. Repro steps below. Can eng take a look? cc @omar-eng @jenna-se :frowning:

omar-eng: Thanks — can you paste the raw client logs and the exact curl we can run? Also whether they're using token refresh (short TTL) or a proxy.

sara-support: Pasting the minimal repro logs they captured (redacted):
```
client: streaming start -> /v1/stream?model=redwood-medium
client-log: SSE received 4 chunks, last chunk:
  data: {"id":"req_0a1b2c","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...and then the user asked about"},"index":0}]}
client-error: read tcp 10.5.3.12:443->198.51.100.23:54022: read: connection reset by peer
sdk: js-client v1.4.2
network: carrier APN=fastdata, NAT type=symmetric (as reported by customer)
```
They also tried websocket and saw the same abrupt FIN after ~30s idle.

jenna-se: That read error + symmetric NAT + mobile carrier makes me suspect port churn / ephemeral NAT eviction. Mobile carriers will often reassign NAT mappings after ~30s of inactivity which looks like a mid-stream drop. Do we have keepalive pings enabled on the SDK by default? If not, we should recommend a heartbeat or smaller flush intervals to keep the flow active. Also ask if the app is backgrounding (Android Doze) — that can suspend sockets.

kai-qa: I repro'd locally on a Pixel 5 with a simulated APN that aggressively times out NAT mappings. Captured tcpdump showing FIN from carrier side ~32s after last data packet:
```
08:42:10.123456 IP 10.5.3.12.54022 > 198.51.100.23.443: Flags [P.], seq 412:856, ack 1024, win 64240
08:42:42.987654 IP 198.51.100.23.443 > 10.5.3.12.54022: Flags [F.], seq 1024, ack 857, win 65535
```
So the server sees a FIN with no graceful closure from client. This matches symmetric NAT eviction where packets start getting routed differently and the carrier responds with a reset/fin.

omar-eng: Thanks Kai — can you confirm whether the server closed or the carrier sent the FIN? If carrier, the runtime will just see the TCP close. We should check our streaming keepalive behavior: do we send occasional 1-byte SSE comments or pings to keep NAT mappings alive? If not, we should add an advisory. @deploy-bot can you check recent runtime config for SSE heartbeat frequency?

deploy-bot: runtime-config-bot: current SSE heartbeat disabled by default for hosted customers to avoid extra tokens. (config id: rc-2026-10)

jenna-se: Ok — two parallel actions:
- Short-term workaround for customer: enable client-side heartbeat/ping every 20s OR switch to websocket streaming with application-level pings. Also implement robust reconnect/resume logic using the last-event-id/resume-token so partial outputs aren't billed or can be resumed.
- Engineering follow-up: enable optional server-side SSE comment pings behind a feature flag for affected customers (keeps NAT mapping alive). Also expose an SDK toggle to opt into aggressive keepalive.

sara-support: Customer asked about billing for partial responses. Can we refund incomplete tokens for sessions terminated mid-stream due to network? They sent several incidents where they received 3/6 responses billed.

omar-eng: Make a ticket (RID-1234) to track engineering work + refund request. For refunds, support should PR a billing credit once we confirm mid-stream disconnects and request_id matches. I'll take the engineering ticket for runtime changes and the SDK toggle.

kai-qa: Created a short test matrix and a reproducer script that toggles NAT timeout and validates we stay connected with 20s client pings. Putting link to gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/testing-sse-nat-repro

sara-support: Sending customer the temporary workaround (20s client heartbeat + resume token) and asking for logs. Will hold billing until we confirm. Thanks all :thumbsup:

omar-eng: Next steps for eng: (1) add optional SSE keepalive feature flag, (2) add telemetry to detect carrier FIN patterns and tag requests so support can auto-detect mid-stream NAT kills, (3) document SDK guidance for mobile clients. I'll assign RID-1234 and add eng-oncall review.
